74C8CEFE980A4731A0E5EE6AD3F33A23.description: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.
comments: For example the expression 1.15<sup>t</sup> can be rewritten as (1.151/12)<sup>12t</sup>  1.012<sup>12t</sup> to reveal the approximate equivalent monhly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.

161A920B096640DB8F2E4B0E57E80092.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.

88E06CA44E58400DAAEBAF6CF53EE027.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.

4AD2259497694681A8B254D7FADCFE32.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.
comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). The star symbol sometimes appears on the heading for a group of standards; in that case, it should be understood to apply to all standards in that group.

CEF4D020E8E04F4BB5B213A0C529B1AD.description: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems

E42BB1B692864D52A69BA0F4DEC3B7B2.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
comments: For example, see x<sup>4</sup> — y<sup>4</sup> as (x²)² — (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² — y²)(x² + y²).

995B7AC045994BB5819DA891D1190E4B.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
comments: For example, interpret P(1+r)<sup>n</sup> as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.

6A1DA1A56EEE47A8B8CD18653FDE6FDD.description: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

DD12D85DC7E04D429AEAE4427FB9B1AE.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context
comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). The star symbol sometimes appears on the heading for a group of standards; in that case, it should be understood to apply to all standards in that group.

A4285272FCD343CF8DBCE0B07284034F.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

8C3692AE679A4B74B00A49C199971AD2.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

B1DE7A52DBE844E9A9D52C4E889E5D28.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

27075B8F820848D983D57D8F8D708212.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

8BFCC9F624114DBD8B30C1F39E7233D9.description: Use words and phrases acquired through conversations, reading and being read to, and responding to texts, including using frequently occurring conjunctions to signal simple relationships (e.g., because).

BFC22C3036C549C988FA3F95F64E3BDA.description: Distinguish shades of meaning among verbs differing in manner (e.g., look, peek, glance, stare, glare, scowl) and adjectives differing in intensity (e.g., large, gigantic) by defining or choosing them or by acting out the meanings.

48CDCAEDD68C4B4882AD8B6A43128FD4.description: Identify real-life connections between words and their use (e.g., note places at home that are cozy).

199809FADEDC49F0AEC38FB86823D45E.description: Define words by category and by one or more key attributes (e.g., a duck is a bird that swims; a tiger is a large cat with stripes).

A9C64C2752824C65BEC4CFF30E25BA39.description: Sort words into categories (e.g., colors, clothing) to gain a sense of the concepts the categories represent.

D6149832B039495EBACBC94491BD7028.description: With guidance and support from adults, demonstrate understanding of word relationships and nuances in word meanings.

755BC1A531884D5581F9479770EFCEC1.description: Identify frequently occurring root words (e.g., look) and their inflectional forms (e.g., looks, looked, looking).

7159281813A1404384A2B1DC028C8248.description: Use frequently occurring affixes as a clue to the meaning of a word.

5392593304F3471B9821DC309DC1B06F.description: Use sentence-level context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

6432FBBE478242989943264B43742062.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 1 reading and content, choosing flexibly from an array of strategies.

856C3C6A078841EFB089C47C5EFF6C31.description: Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on phonemic awareness and spelling conventions.

6CAA45DBDFA64838B0744CB1468C92C7.description: Use conventional spelling for words with common spelling patterns and for frequently occurring irregular words.

2C3604A2A7454F84A2550DA3ABB791E2.description: Use commas in dates and to separate single words in a series.

218D8BCC9F91488193A6C4F92492A644.description: Capitalize dates and names of people.

E96639EA8D474A4CA959F62E863F2638.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

C87F832EF0E94E02990D79EC5FC6BA01.description: Produce and expand complete simple and compound declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences in response to prompts.

30C76678C01D42B98F1509E453E2995A.description: Use frequently occurring prepositions (e.g., during, beyond, toward).

88C47D1E51D84A81ABA1008691A01CF9.description: Use frequently occurring conjunctions (e.g., and, but, or, so, because).

10029285FF6D4092B3A567A5F9B0E0F3.description: Use verbs to convey a sense of past, present, and future (e.g., Yesterday I walked home; Today I walk home; Tomorrow I will walk home).

10029285FF6D4092B3A567A5F9B0E0F2.description: Use personal, possessive, and indefinite pronouns (e.g., I, me, my; they, them, their; anyone, everything).

1B7E77E79A694A50825B27446D25B0A7.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in basic sentences (e.g., He hops; We hop).

1B7E77E79A694A50825B27446D25B0A6.description: Use common, proper, and possessive nouns.

445E2005937F4C27BDD22984651B07D2.description: Print all upper- and lowercase letters.

C34A7209EE3E4969AA850420FEC6523F.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

937AF931E36749BFA8D750801593B47B.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

8B9A634942C544D0807022913E991E0B.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

233CB3C683F74A53B67D35424CD09C86.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

5F1784E912904BF7B35A6C158E9C3FF0.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

876BBC4E087749BB9226532A09C99807.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

3665FC38700F441E856312C158E6E15D.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

CC22CBA0DFE401311AFB68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

56484E758B0C493BB6A13BCA8693BCE8.description: Produce complete sentences when appropriate to task and situation.

F3F519B42B7B47E790C1DAF58088E1F1.description: Add drawings or other visual displays to descriptions when appropriate to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

6E2D016E2DDA44C692C914038ADDF840.description: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas and feelings clearly.

273C443CA80448C187AC723D748BEAD0.description: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.

F3EE7C8F23F24126BD0651730CB58A1E.description: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

3748A21AC5BA4441973C6825F396BC40.description: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.

50099228DF4B4023AB83F7289D75B1E4.description: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.

31B991750C6C44BF87FB225613634AF8.description: Follow agreed-upon rules for discussions (e.g., listening to others with care, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).

14BCFED58745444588E0F1E24E6844D8.description: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about grade 1 topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups

BC0EFAD74E2143ABADC1CA0369789602.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

4C8F2FD31ADF4546B232A5738D68E877.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

630BF73EC0E145C3A7F96A7B3C9D6C7F.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

76E787D21B184CB0AB82D3F875D9C9EF.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

06B74969ACF5415593729E5F72520B95.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

9E1029AB3A2A4158A86352A222BF9CFA.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

CC2089C0DFE401311AF868A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

0E67324E20F14A2E9BDF4494707FF952.description: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.

D067DF52C66F4F79BCE0170F02BF264D.description: Participate in shared research and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of "how-to" books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).

CC07C7C0DFE401311AE768A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

225073A1EEB542ABB0B60251B1D26F5B.description: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers.

53656DAB5C544D149250293649639FDD.description: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.

0E6E3191AE3E42C7A035F122382B2FE6.description: Write narratives in which they recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some details regarding what happened, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide some sense of closure.

92358B29DE0547FC8F72FA598178CE1D.description: Write informative/explanatory texts in which they name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.

FAC60846470941288709BFAC1B2E78A7.description: Write opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or name the book they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.

36D8C18FEE9A4D1EA23B152826A46BD6.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences.

715BA2820AE24BE3A36F2E0A464A2478.description: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

AEFE3EEAE3BB47E2AEEAD0734A600CFC.description: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility and accuracy of each source, and integrate the information while avoiding plagiarism.

67E93A9216AF4AB1833D7EFE5E1BA3F3.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects based on focused questions, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

CC278E10DFE401311B0268A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

1BB18CCD34DC48058A295A03C8E81018.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing and to interact and collaborate with others.

84CA382EE8BC44BCAAA5435592D29C51.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.

1ADBB297077942C19F9B14B2A672758D.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

A37F77A3B9DE4704902FB3276C884E04.description: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, well-chosen details, and well-structured event sequences.

58D69C8308E840DDAC416F88B79DB048.description: Write informative/explanatory texts to examine and convey complex ideas and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content.

41A80E92004349F8BF89F9368C768670.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

CC254DF0DFE401311AFF68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Writing

D5DD0989FE224AA4894E3365CBB72AEA.description: Use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

29ED4571793F4804B52C2446096B2732.description: Read on-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

B687A93F788A452E825B7C22ECD18123.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).

7F21B27D0DC44C42BCF0BC71A209E666.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category) to better understand each of the words.

B522C234B95C4186A8B6BD571792B619.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification) in context.

6195E2E8571F4572B6070C6193A2D89F.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

8A410795B8AA4ABE976FC1FC160438CE.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

7A16B17F238C4C8A8888F9F0E64B479E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

F2FFF1B3913D4161B28EE71282200129.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).

D6A14868A9384900AD95513ECF478BE7.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

11624E00396A49809AEB098BB3F00129.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

355EA55021354F1CB7EA0C112584D876.description: Maintain consistency in style and tone.

B87BE93FE3874E6C939E8F6A86BA3384.description: Vary sentence patterns for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

A4DF66EFF99A4AFAB85BA92C6FB9947D.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

A5F5C11211974E41B42E84D75E950258.description: Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive/parenthetical elements.

79B22369712E49D6B5C01FBA75D5EF17.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

F3A4D50BBECB4999A6EAE3020915092B.description: Recognize variations from standard English in their own and others' writing and speaking, and identify and use strategies to improve expression in conventional language.

C0CD7732829C44B49B7617BD533D8A16.description: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (i.e., ones with unclear or ambiguous antecedents).

1E3C050891F445208F92CC64A6301CDC.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

A807D254795643C0BAAEE57510605B4F.description: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive).

BF4D7D5368EC481D8A0F93327A9F021A.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

CDD7E560DFE401311BDC68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

00C6E0D757AC4A5D87733F67E5181111.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

71FC15A762054A55A70C295F066329FB.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

1336ADD375A1408FBDC2C38C284B7A46.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

0528496CE6064011B694A44266198DC4.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

F06BFEDFDC584D7ABB26C4FC8C7C68E9.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

CDD57A30DFE401311BD868A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

64FD51AD5762431695A76D4AB4A4D37D.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

E44993EAC7534D919C49EC24DCE8460B.description: Include multimedia components (e.g., graphics, images, music, sound) and visual displays in presentations to clarify information.

4CE9837CED3E4A5D9B856C5EDF03288A.description: Present claims and findings, sequencing ideas logically and using pertinent descriptions, facts, and details to accentuate main ideas or themes; use appropriate eye contact, adequate volume, and clear pronunciation.

E10776D426E14E7B8E717D8C2C2C6ED7.description: Delineate a speaker's argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

790C05ACC29A464480530E1E2B91FDE9.description: Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) and explain how it contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.

F5A1CBE243A44F8A9C73BAC3FF89826A.description: Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate understanding of multiple perspectives through reflection and paraphrasing.

4EA2FAFCC5CE46BC9DF93097DA947444.description: Pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail by making comments that contribute to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.

8950E735FFB9467BA903BB30BD8EDC41.description: Follow rules for collegial discussions, set specific goals and deadlines, and define individual roles as needed.

DC2BB986F60746D69DB78581BF8FF2F5.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read or studied required material; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue to probe and reflect on ideas under discussion.

274BD335455344E8A7FB38E7DC665C4B.description: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grade 6 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly.

DDD58C3829E74E9D9001C8E3A7BD2438.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

214BD5F3E8E34008BE40D3A5B6E2ABD9.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

386BBA7376BF49C98A6761A8E080AAF0.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

D7E04319241D45C782F003C275B488BA.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

94CD8F2860894E6497D7DC58EB3C44C4.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

71F2975F30BF4075B015F0C403ED383F.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

CDD31350DFE401311BD568A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

CE3EA2ECF5E844829F95D0B06AC27D31.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

B2DA5A87301342CDB023AC470C5C9BBD.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

DD198317186D4E9597FA8F528E78D620.description: Conduct short research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question), drawing on several sources and generating additional related, focused questions that allow for multiple avenues of exploration.

CDF18240DFE401311BEF68A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

C9E22CABD9BA47FD98CB981DC8C038BD.description: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on how well purpose and audience have been addressed.

28C31C3B859742F8B1D75DDDFF4E30A8.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

34E7AFC8EF9D46E88724E6998C0EAD89.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented.

5A390B3D34394A2389881BD7297BAB67.description: Write arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence.

3BC761F3BD634978B866E9E9D06E6FB6.description: Determine the central ideas or conclusions of a text; provide an accurate summary of the text distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

52C2E819308E437984655AC70E6AA574.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of science and technical texts.

64AF8FDF465C4374811019034340FA20.description: By the end of grade 8, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 6—8 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

A697F5F2D90A48BEA6D0ED2B99521D85.description: Analyze the relationship between a primary and secondary source on the same topic.

03EFAD777DD7459CA3A5013DE7DCCC11.description: Distinguish among fact, opinion, and reasoned judgment in a text.

7346BD7C90EF4C80B5BBE7AAD899AAD0.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary specific to domains related to history/social studies.

043BDC13460240B9AC83AC760BF7F913.description: Identify key steps in a text's description of a process related to history/social studies (e.g., how a bill becomes law, how interest rates are raised or lowered).

CA14403CBAA64688B886E7EDCB0043F9.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of the source distinct from prior knowledge or opinions.

D7735279C3B249C486A49F8AB51A5DA6.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources.

4BD3C10AF2A443549F2E7D3FEFE3BC07.description: By the end of the year, read and comprehend literary nonfiction in the grades 6—8 text complexity band proficiently, with scaffolding as needed at the high end of the range.

827F6B6FD3DA40F1B66176C00BD996E9.description: Trace and evaluate the argument and specific claims in a text, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.

22D179F16A704EE4AF18DC2384BAE80F.description: Analyze how a particular sentence, paragraph, chapter, or section fits into the overall structure of a text and contributes to the development of the ideas.

6AB05BAE008346DEBCC18C5DEB7E9F6D.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including figurative, connotative, and technical meanings.

E1359871E8F64176AC380DBA0DE92C80.description: Analyze in detail how a key individual, event, or idea is introduced, illustrated, and elaborated in a text (e.g., through examples or anecdotes).

17A23339A48B465FAE962DA539664AFF.description: Introduce a topic clearly, previewing what is to follow; organize ideas, concepts, and information into broader categories as appropriate to achieving purpose; include formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., charts, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension.

76B770D9F14C4CA4B9C241E796D277A9.description:
6. Usan las palabras y las frases que han aprendido
a través de conversaciones, al leer y al escuchar
cuando se les lee, o al responder a los textos,
incluyendo el uso de adjetivos y adverbios para
describir (ejemplo: Cuando otros niños están
contentos yo también me siento contento).

BEC82B7329AC4BDCABA81CE8D64E5BA9.description:
b. Distinguen los matices de significado entre
verbos estrechamente relacionados (ejemplo:
tirar, aventar, lanzar) y adjetivos estrechamente
relacionados (ejemplo: delgado, esbelto, flaco).

3D76397AEE044FDA87300604293E5C73.description:
a. Identifican las conexiones en la vida real entre las
palabras y su uso (ejemplo: describen alimentos
que son picantes o jugosos)

93E725A7587F4F349C10FAEA8457CB49.description:
5. Demuestran comprensión de relación entre las
palabras y sus matices de significado.

44323FF968314F5489C35A13315D38B4.description:
e. Usan glosarios y diccionarios básicos, tanto
impresos como digitales, para determinar o aclarar
el significado de palabras y frases.

7B250C59CF0749E29E406A5F524ADA73.description:
d. Usan el conocimiento del significado de palabras
simples para predecir el significado de palabras
compuestas (ejemplo: pasar, pasatiempo; sacar,
sacapuntas, bien, bienvenidos).

053085269ECC45A1B860872ECA642400.description:
c. Usan una palabra de raíz conocida como clave
para entender el significado de una palabra
desconocida con la misma raíz (ejemplo: adición,
adicional).

65FE8A63DA0741ECAEF9A6898C003011.description:
b. Determinan el significado de una nueva palabra
formada cuando un prefijo conocido se le añade
a una palabra conocida (ejemplo: feliz-infeliz,
contar-recontar).

3493916EA5174A2E8BA327A6859F46C0.description:
a. Usan el contexto de la oración para entender el
significado de una palabra o frase.

B1D53BC74B9E40068D159446FF9888A4.description:
4. Determinan y aclaran el significado de palabras y
frases desconocidas y de palabras de significados
múltiples en base a la lectura y el contenido
académico de segundo grado, eligiendo con
flexibilidad entre una serie de estrategias.

93F14C15A44442B2A8929F81803E216C.description: a. Comparan el uso formal e informal del español.

54E432C3AACE48FB9BE382400D8ECFB9.description:

al escribir, hablar, leer o escuchar.

14FC9608CF1B492AB73F54E46FE76548.description:
g. Categorizan palabras de acuerdo con su acento
tónico (agudas, graves y esdrújulas) y emplean el
acento escrito (acento ortográfico) en palabras ya
conocida

296D965DA0AF41BDB0D9B1FA74C74ADE.description:
f. Utilizan el guión corto para separar las sílabas de
una palabra (ma-ri-po-sa); para indicar nivel, gama o
intervalos (enero-marzo; de 1:00 p. m. - 3:00 p. m.)
y el guión largo para introducir un diálogo.

90667DE7C13C482FB41D63B5EFDA8DF2.description:
e. Consultan materiales de referencia, incluyendo
diccionarios básicos, según sea necesario
para revisar y corregir la ortografía o consultar
traducciones.

FA51A90289C843629A026FED11210B7F.description:
d. Generalizan los patrones ortográficos al escribir
y forman y usan sustantivos que en plural sufren
cambios ortográficos (feliz g felices;
carácter g caracteres).

D7063660C02545BBA1A007B959994759.description:
c. Usan las contracciones del y al correctamente
y reconocen la preposición “de” para señalar
posesión.

7760CE3A2A3A443D8FADE22FD4CE8EAA.description:
b. Usan dos puntos y aparte en el saludo de una carta;
y una coma en la despedida de una carta escrita
en español. Reconocen que se usa una coma en el
saludo y la despedida de una carta en inglés.

599357BB4FA94C95A54D5DCC9019699C.description:
a. Emplean la mayúscula al escribir nombres propios,
días festivos, marcas de productos, nombres
geográficos y sólo en la primera letra de títulos de
libros, películas, obras teatrales, etc.

52DF03A656BF4CF9BC8882AA37676AD8.description:

español para el uso de las letras mayúsculas, signos
de puntuación y ortografía.

9F1B2B653A3C404CAAB7C95BC572FE98.description:
f. Producen, elaboran y reorganizan oraciones
completas, simples y compuestas (ejemplo: El niño
vio la película. El niño pequeño vio la película. La
película que vio el niño pequeño fue interesante.).

4CE312C79E094FA59FC142D528815FC1.description:

dependiendo de lo que se va a modificar. (ejemplo:
rápido, rápidamente, lento, lentamente).

2B71060CE4F94A38AF164FE8A4D766CF.description:
d. Forman y usan el tiempo pasado de los verbos
irregulares que se utilizan con frecuencia (ejemplo:
decir-dijo, hacer-hizo, poner-puso, saber-supimos).

98EAF00EF7734593935FCC3C157D3684.description:
c. Usan los pronombres reflexivos (ejemplo:
Me lavo las manos. Nos cansamos mucho. Se
sienten contentos hoy).

4136AE0259D94BF2AEC428864EEDA122.description:
a. Usan sustantivos colectivos (ejemplo:
la gente, el grupo).

BA616B2D398246C7B32E937B1B3955A3.description:

gramática del español y su uso al escribir y al hablar.

24169D75C24945D59E9B8E1661370E18.description:
6. Escriben oraciones completas cuando es adecuado
a la tarea y situación, a fin de proporcionar detalles
solicitados o aclaraciones. (Ver los estándares 1-3
de lenguaje para expectativas adicionales).

6011EAB317C549A4855F889E2C26B142.description:
5. Hacen grabaciones de audio de cuentos o poemas;

cuentos o relatan experiencias cuando es adecuado,
para aclarar ideas, pensamientos y sentimientos.

0862A148E14A41A6A69CF4CEEF19F505.description:

con hechos apropiados y detalles descriptivos

coherentes.

018451A3A0FD4C308B0329F832E208C6.description:

obtener información adicional o profundizar en la
comprensión del tema o asunto.

E88B9D6F3DAC4917A10E7320CB89040F.description:
2. Recuentan o describen las ideas clave y los detalles
de un texto leído en voz alta, o de información
presentada oralmente o a través de otros medios de
comunicación.

74DEF9F90C1B4DC881D4CB97B15023F1.description:
c. Solicitan aclaración y una explicación más
detallada, cuando es necesario, sobre los temas y
los textos que se están tratando.

D12B1F27A3CD44118E60942C93FBD96F.description:
b. Toman en cuenta lo que los demás dicen en
conversaciones, mediante el enlace de sus
comentarios a las observaciones de los demás.

0D0052CBA893403BB152363201BABFD4.description:
a. Siguen las reglas acordadas para participar en
conversaciones (por ejemplo: tomar la palabra de
una manera respetuosa, escuchar a los demás
con atención, hablar uno a la vez sobre los temas
y textos que se están tratando).

63F041B1CD5C412A968E4A5D9765CCFC.description:

 conocimientos

3C7B6814B7A34916AD90F3D4E8E0EA4D.description:

C17110BE2B7147E09C41FB1F5397C156.description:

DDA50C44BC1D4DB49AF2B9F010EE5B23.description:

98485EE85F034CCA95A04D037C3336BE.description:

varios párrafos, así como el enfoque de párrafos
específicos en el texto.

E32BD2C435C040B193AF8B611DA4A398.description:
1. Hacen y contestan preguntas tales como: quién, qué,

DE TEXTO INFORMATIVO

1A858E137D2C4E52BC84B750FB59FDA4.description: Nivel de lectura y de complejidad del texto

mismo cuento (por ejemplo: cuentos de Cenicienta)

7. Usan la información obtenida de las ilustraciones y

importantes.

77D4CD390CAB4ABBA93A2F9EA6F8BFB1.description:
2. Recuentan cuentos, incluyendo fábulas y cuentos

1. Hacen y contestan preguntas tales como: quién, qué,

C1D1C6D66A544A7D9496DE5196B83316.description:
a. Ordenan las palabras en categorías
(ejemplo: colores, ropa) para obtener un sentido
de los conceptos que representan las categorías.

F4DA8F2909AE486BB0466833082E8626.description:
5. Con la orientación y el apoyo de adultos, demuestran
comprensión de las relaciones entre las palabras y
sus matices de significado.

2EE560E213394DEEAE72335AD9DB89B8.description:
c. Identifican la raíz de las palabras de uso frecuente
(por ejemplo: mirar) y sus formas de inflexión
(ejemplo: miradas, miró, mirando).

ECBFFD0E50EF476E8C0EAEAD6B63C007.description:
b. Usan los afijos de uso frecuente para entender el
significado de una palabra.

5F80AF789703497EB8408643E7A3329B.description:
a. Usan el contexto de la oración para entender el
significado de una palabra o frase.

37A6EEC49E87405591264CB7DB893C1B.description:
4. Determinan o aclaran el significado de palabras y
frases desconocidas y de palabras y frases con
significados múltiples, en base a la lectura y el
contenido académico de primer grado, eligiendo con
flexibilidad entre una serie de estrategias.

C031D3349CA3495CBAA26A1B5B949EA6.description:
f. Reconocen el acento escrito en palabras sencillas
y ya conocidas (mamá, papá, José).

FC6B23CF39A94C9DBEF585AEF0F2EFAC.description:
e. Deletrean fonéticamente palabras desconocidas,
usando la fonética, el reconocimiento de palabras
y las normativas de la ortografía.

5EA0F4558F084DB397C25F2B0D806459.description:
d. Usan ortografía convencional para palabras con
patrones ortográficos comunes y para palabras de
ortografía compleja de uso frecuente.

3F5C1EFECE154887AEDDCCAAEA9AE924.description:
c. Reconocen la función de la coma para enumerar y
separar palabras en una serie.

7B5EE8F2ED0941C4A853ED5F9A001A8A.description:
b. Usan la puntuación correcta para empezar
y/o finalizar las oraciones, incluyendo el uso
correcto de los signos de interrogación ¿?; y de
exclamación ¡!.

37035E62B9564C04AC296163D96CCD0E.description:
a. Emplean la mayúscula al escribir nombres de
personas, lugares, nombres de días festivos
(Navidad, Año Nuevo, etc.) y eventos importantes
(Cinco de Mayo).

E744D1556B0343DFA17CB6AEB56363C7.description:
2. Demuestran al escribir dominio de las normativas del
español para el uso de las letras mayúsculas, signos
de puntuación y ortografía.

CB53917CE0424625848C0C6C0DEB9035.description:
l. Reconocen y explican la formación de las dos
contracciones del español: al = a + el,
del = de + el.

A58935057B2140B9BA8EB84275DDF247.description:
k. Leen palabras compuestas (abrelatas, anteojos,
sacapuntas) y separan las dos palabras que las
componen.

672714B991E247928C95B56D7FC35929.description:
j. Producen y elaboran oraciones declarativas,
interrogativas, imperativas y exclamativas, simples
y compuestas al responder a sugerencias o pautas.

BCD62F309E3045F59B347ED3A78319DE.description:
i. Usan correctamente las preposiciones que se
utilizan con frecuencia (ejemplo: sin, según,
desde, hasta, hacia).

2FBFC46E320E42CF9FE9825A7AAEF439.description:
h. Usan determinativos tales como los artículos
o pronombres demostrativos, reconociendo la
concordancia de género y número (ejemplo: los
libros, esos libros; las niñas, aquellas niñas).

5EB6EE67D0E34031A2412C6B70D7B63B.description:
g. Usan conjunciones que se utilizan con frecuencia
(ejemplo: y, pero, o, así que, porque).

EADAC8D08A524917BF916BBAECF54882.description:
f. Usan adjetivos que se utilizan con frecuencia
notando concordancia de género y número con
el sustantivo.

09E40ABE320F4FA39B6C8832231F994D.description:
e. Usan verbos regulares para comunicar la noción
del tiempo pasado, presente y futuro (ejemplo:
Ayer caminé a casa. Hoy camino a casa. Mañana
caminaré a casa).

58D18A69D15D425D8DB2BB2C166371E6.description:
d. Usan pronombres personales, pronombres
posesivos e indefinidos (yo, me, mi, mío, alguien).
Reconocen el uso formal e informal entre
tú/usted.

3B27392CE7C240608A69EBA84F99F7B8.description:
c. Usan el sustantivo en su forma singular o plural
empleando la concordancia correcta entre
sustantivo y verbo en oraciones básicas
(ejemplo: el niño brinca; los niños brincan).

8909461374B84F558A990AA80E8F1432.description: b. Usan sustantivos comunes y propios.

8FD09B84C9FF4C7F938C0AA49E76EB7C.description:
a. Escriben con letra de molde todas las letras
mayúsculas y minúsculas.

3BABACD57B6F4C659B6B162B34B64497.description:
1. Demuestran dominio de las normativas de la
gramática del español y su uso al escribir y al hablar.

895A03BE131B4BA0A33C32E52F3975DD.description:
6. Forman oraciones completas cuando es adecuado
según la tarea y situación.

ECB59027E4D0460DAC0A86E57428548F.description:
5. Añaden dibujos u otros medios visuales a las
descripciones cuando es adecuado, para aclarar
ideas, pensamientos y sentimientos.

E7B8B197E4464779A55738993639CB46.description:
4. Describen a personas, lugares, cosas y
acontecimientos con detalles relevantes, expresando
sus ideas y sentimientos con claridad.

AD9069841A254AAC83601EEA56EA5CF5.description: Presentación de conocimientos y de ideas

09D529B637CD4455AD3F8F755761D815.description:
3. Hacen y contestan preguntas sobre lo que dice quien
habla a fin de obtener información adicional o aclarar
algo que no se entiende.

9464974D7AFB45B98560C8923D66B87C.description:
2. Hacen y contestan preguntas sobre los detalles
clave en un texto leído en voz alta, o información
presentada oralmente o a través de otros medios de
comunicación.

73D494B138DF4ABCA4EF453F94A60F9C.description:
c. Hacen preguntas para aclarar cualquier confusión
sobre los temas y los textos que
se están tratando.

CC208A0E7C504B378F4E081AA495C761.description:
b. Toman en cuenta lo que los demás dicen en
conversaciones, respondiendo a los comentarios
que otros hacen a través de múltiples intercambios.

0B0358399DC34137A1E3548130311924.description:
a. Siguen las reglas acordadas para participar en
conversaciones (por ejemplo: escuchar a los
demás con atención, hablar uno a la vez sobre los
temas y textos que se están tratando).

2B0F9674A0FE49A3B52DFE54F99DFED9.description:
1. Participan en conversaciones colaborativas con
diversos compañeros y adultos en grupos pequeños
y grandes sobre temas y textos apropiados al primer
grado.

27F402B102B44941A6E64F23BE1F63DE.description:
PRIMER GRADO
ESTÁNDARES DE AUDICIÓN
Y EXPRESIÓN ORAL

B18254FC1C364F308D7536567DC12DF2.description:
8. Con la orientación y el apoyo de adultos, recuerdan
información de experiencias o recopilan información
de diversas fuentes que se les ofrece para contestar
una pregunta.

5695B2F996514F4D887081BDD14D333B.description:
7. Participan en proyectos compartidos de investigación
y escritura (por ejemplo: exploran una serie de libros
sobre “cómo funciona” o “cómo se hace algo”,
sobre un tema determinado y los usan para escribir
una secuencia de instrucciones).

C96FE31C75C94933BDB4B0A39A6B70CA.description:
Investigación para la formación y presentación de
 conocimientos

7D3930ECE4524ED188562D61196458E0.description:
6. Con la orientación y el apoyo de adultos, usan una
variedad de herramientas digitales para producir y
publicar escritos, incluso en colaboración con sus
compañeros.

D6231F3F67CB48BEB29F1B4B22FE6195.description:
5. Con la orientación y el apoyo de adultos, se
enfocan en un tema, responden a las preguntas y
sugerencias de sus compañeros y añaden detalles
para mejorar el escrito según sea necesario.

256FC765AE9540FA92B743E3327B7CFD.description: Producción y redacción de la escritura

C676A30A40934A61A717C0673675FE0C.description:
3. Escriben narraciones en las cuales recuentan dos
o más acontecimientos en secuencia adecuada,
incluyen algunos detalles relacionados con lo que
sucedió, usan palabras que describen el tiempo para
señalar el orden de los acontecimientos y ofrecen
cierto sentido de conclusión.

77F57FFBB48E473691E3C4729C567769.description:
2. Escriben textos informativos y explicativos en los
cuales identifican un tema, ofrecen algunos datos
sobre dicho tema y proveen cierto sentido de
conclusión.

971E2DD98B4E4481B96CA05363C035E5.description:
1. Escriben propuestas de opinión en las cuales
presentan el tema o título del libro sobre el cual están
escribiendo, expresan su opinión, ofrecen la razón
para esa opinión y cierto sentido de conclusión.

0D287B9E75D748BDB961F23AE843B306.description: Tipos de textos y sus propósitos

E66FCD68443140B5AD87B02B152DD24C.description:

ESTÁNDARES DE ESCRITURA
Y REDACCIÓN

0AA2FE1659B240D9B133DCB1FB6D5A57.description:
c. Usan el contexto para confirmar o autocorregir el
reconocimiento de las palabras y la comprensión,
releyendo cuando sea necesario.

25BECF219EED4D6A95249FB073AB9D5F.description:
b. Leen oralmente textos a nivel de grado con
precisión, ritmo adecuado y expresión en lecturas
sucesivas.

8EA18D43F4CC4340A537861CB158717F.description:
a. Leen textos a nivel de grado, con propósito
y comprensión.

99529AD5654C4C4889ED9A31EC4119FF.description:
4. Leen con suficiente precisión y fluidez para apoyar
la comprensión.

E87044B5C47549088B5C2A66D1291DAB.description:
j. Reconocen que el acento escrito (acento
ortográfico) es una marca colocada sobre una
vocal que indica cuál es la sílaba de mayor énfasis
de la palabra y que sigue las reglas ortográficas.

A59BAA4203DD41499AFA4CC1C16C1DE8.description:
i. Distinguen entre las vocales y las consonantes
y reconocen que sólo las vocales llevan acento
escrito.

433D045FA8F54C74962871BE4C3FE9B9.description:
h. Reconocen combinaciones consonánticas
(consonante + l; consonante + r ) en palabras ya
conocidas que contienen letras líquidas (blanco,
planta, grande, tronco, traspaso, claro, trabajo,
otra, cuatro).

A116A16901CE41308A38837F94D3D2C2.description:
f. Leen palabras con inflexiones al final (género
-o/-a; número –os/-as, aumentativos –ote y
diminutivos -ito).

1FEDFA4F282C4C928699F6FF6510F14D.description:
e. Decodifican palabras de dos y tres sílabas
siguiendo patrones básicos al dividir las palabras
en sílabas.

4D1B1BD1CC40477C9AAB5177B6DF1FC1.description:
d. Usan el conocimiento de que toda sílaba debe de
tener por lo menos el sonido de una vocal para
determinar el número de sílabas en una palabra
escrita (ejemplo: sílabas con una sola vocal,
diptongos o triptongos).

D20FCF06B3584495B7E630341FFC7A38.description:
c. Distinguen entre las vocales fuertes (a,e,o) y las
vocales débiles (i,u) que se juntan en una sílaba
para formar diptongo.

AFD31935896542D9828486A99FE9791F.description:
b. Distinguen entre las sílabas abiertas (terminadas
en vocal) y las sílabas cerradas (terminadas en
consonante).

ADB0766B41D24185B9CEC7205D7AA72C.description:
a. Conocen la correlación grafo-fónica para los tres
dígrafos consonánticos: ch, ll, rr (chile, lluvia,
perro).

0320F365953F43C9B31D5FAAA1644E7D.description:
3. Conocen y aplican la fonética y las destrezas
de análisis de palabras al nivel de grado, en la
decodificación de palabras.

EDAD75D1283A4CB6B8903CAFF086061E.description:
f. Distinguen oralmente los sonidos de las vocales
en una sola sílaba que forman un diptongo (auto,
lluvia, agua, aire, ciudad).

89066C82A316496A930D7E8457C3249C.description:
e. Dividen palabras bisílabas CVCV en las sílabas
que las componen: me-sa, ca-ma, ca-sa, pe-ro,
ga-to

244175FAF8C54141B8D85832C635F3B5.description:
d. Dividen palabras monosilábicas en secuencia
completa por sus sonidos individuales (fonemas).

0E7A8F30627943AE9AEEDE6F53564320.description:
c. Separan y pronuncian fonemas tales como la vocal
inicial y media y los sonidos finales en palabras
pronunciadas oralmente de una sola sílaba
(monosilábicas).

171ECF174ED4450F9CD4A3C9A7A733B4.description:
b. Forman oralmente palabras de una sílaba
al combinar sonidos (fonemas), incluyendo
combinaciones de consonantes (las, mar, sal).

DB1A401F6AED48E48899DCE29DF55726.description:
a. Distinguen los sonidos (fonemas) de las vocales
en palabras.

2151656B7ED64E27808CF5083439C63E.description:
2. Demuestran comprensión de las palabras
pronunciadas oralmente, las sílabas y los sonidos
(fonemas).

A29F2C0D6ADC43AE99BEA5B79B6AC2E5.description:
c. Reconocen que el acento escrito indica a veces
un significado distinto en palabras que se escriben
con las mismas letras (si, sí; te, té; tu, tú); en ese
caso se llama acento diacrítico.

484C13A3197D4F64A3539F7531639FC9.description:
b. Reconocen que el acento escrito (acento
ortográfico) es una marca que se llama tilde
colocada sobre una vocal y que indica dónde recae
el énfasis de la palabra.

59506780487245458ADFEEBE55FB5D17.description:
a. Reconocen las características de una oración, por
ejemplo: uso de mayúsculas en la primera palabra,
puntuación final, uso de los signos de interrogación
(¿?), exclamación (¡!), y guión largo para abrir y
cerrar un diálogo.

40BA08A61C104BE7AD2B25C9ECEBEB37.description:
1. Demuestran comprensión de la organización y
características básicas de los materiales impresos.

22F71C0AFC8C450EBF0B0F8F74D70AEE.description:
PRIMER GRADO
ESTÁNDARES DE LECTURA:
DESTREZAS FUNDAMENTALES

62186CB6A453408DBD75F0027EC2EAF5.description:
10. Con sugerencias y apoyo, leen textos informativos
de complejidad apropiada para el primer grado.

0573024A1B8842E9B0B9F59AB63D29C0.description: Nivel de lectura y de complejidad del texto

937308E3806542A99EC3229EB5CB90B9.description:
9. Identifican las semejanzas y diferencias básicas entre

ilustraciones, descripciones o procedimientos).

78B3EFAD33B246FFB32945E5EE1B3E32.description:
8. Identifican las razones que un autor ofrece para
apoyar los puntos en un texto.

E37A696C91304A41B2CC59D4259C536A.description:
7. Usan las ilustraciones y los detalles en un texto para
describir las ideas clave.

1301C86FFFC04176948550B0F897D521.description:
6. Distinguen entre la información proporcionada por
imágenes u otras ilustraciones y la información
contenida en las palabras de un texto.

C35467203D084EE28EFA83C741BED870.description:
5. Conocen y usan varias características de texto
(por ejemplo: encabezados, tablas de contenido,
glosarios, menús electrónicos, iconos), para localizar
los datos clave o información en un texto.

1E92E4C466CF48C383081100E883E692.description:
4. Hacen y contestan preguntas para determinar o
aclarar el significado de palabras y frases en un texto.

2A769CADB1B9448A9F6B6FAB72C5E400.description:
3. Describen la relación entre dos personas,
acontecimientos, ideas, o elementos de información
en un texto.

48F7E016C30941E7921BDE6BB626F435.description:
2. Identifican el tema principal y recuentan los detalles
clave de un texto.

FCFF2C7817034324917BA2B220ECF123.description:
1. Hacen y contestan preguntas sobre los detalles clave
en un texto.

FBBFC43641CC481094F1291ACD1D54EA.description:

ESTÁNDARES DE LECTURA
PARA TEXTO INFORMATIVO

EB5214526F454863AEEC3424C2E7D05C.description:
10. Con sugerencias y apoyo, leen prosa y poesía
de complejidad apropiada para el primer grado.
complejidad apropiada para el primer grado.

4096FEE04DEC4A36A9DD101F78D2F8ED.description: Nivel de lectura y de complejidad del texto

62179A0125E94B7994D663AFC6FBD2A3.description:
9. Comparan y contrastan las aventuras y experiencias
de los personajes en los cuentos.

528C762309544F64BE408E5AB182D243.description:
7. Usan las ilustraciones y detalles de un cuento
para describir a los personajes, ambientes o
acontecimientos.

D804A7D17E7A458C8AB491EA4F93CE32.description:
6. Identifican al narrador del cuento en varios momentos
del texto.

CC5E2AE4E9164E9FBEA743480FF292E3.description:
5. Explican las diferencias principales entre libros de
cuentos y libros que ofrecen información, usando
una amplia variedad de lectura en diferentes tipos
de texto.

EEC88A94CBB544C8BDAF86216658336A.description:
4. Identifican palabras y frases en cuentos o poemas
que sugieren sentimientos o apelan a los sentidos.

125814424C72443FAE08B94861873E67.description:
3. Describen personajes, ambientes y acontecimientos
importantes en un cuento, usando detalles clave.

456543BC19EC45FA99FBA6144B5C2419.description:
2. Recuentan cuentos, incluyendo los detalles clave,
y demuestran comprensión del mensaje principal o
lección.

E0AD7F10A4354953BC51A96FF4B28D20.description:
1. Hacen y contestan preguntas sobre los detalles clave
de un texto.

standardSets.subject: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies

document.title: Common Core ELA Standards

D0963360301F4918BEDF103DC75774D0.description: By the end of grade 12, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 11-CCR text complexity band independently and proficiently.

22F680F8B8A140F4973AD0CECC108BBF.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

7AC7F26F517847948B3F5A1B7F1CA500.description: Integrate information from diverse sources, both primary and secondary, into a coherent understanding of an idea or event, noting discrepancies among sources.

D5A40D0A2636424F96C3A0899CCD7B22.description: Evaluate an author's premises, claims, and evidence by corroborating or challenging them with other information.

736DE3D655514466956CC48E170BFD19.description: Integrate and evaluate multiple sources of information presented in diverse formats and media (e.g., visually, quantitatively, as well as in words) in order to address a question or solve a problem.

D5A36FFF54C34691B238FABD4EAC2502.description: Evaluate authors' differing points of view on the same historical event or issue by assessing the authors' claims, reasoning, and evidence.

3D485853581C4F0B8983F0A28CAE49E2.description: Analyze in detail how a complex primary source is structured, including how key sentences, paragraphs, and larger portions of the text contribute to the whole.

060D6F8B1345407F83D848D2426B692C.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including analyzing how an author uses and refines the meaning of a key term over the course of a text (e.g., how Madison defines faction in Federalist No. 10).

B94202F284904725B79CDAB18C93394F.description: Evaluate various explanations for actions or events and determine which explanation best accords with textual evidence, acknowledging where the text leaves matters uncertain.

CD13E04516D1415D8D1EA7D12B6A6E4C.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary that makes clear the relationships among the key details and ideas.

DAA91986DEAE4469874C21F85F30F65E.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, connecting insights gained from specific details to an understanding of the text as a whole.

standardSets.subject: Reading Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies

document.title: English Language Arts - History/Social Studies

A440C82F19D44A149984CDCD85C1A712.description: By the end of grade 10, read and comprehend history/social studies texts in the grades 9-10 text complexity band independently and proficiently.

E9B8A2610D7148D4AB41FA2F7DD553E9.description: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity

E4A61C0162DB4F1C9345C2179D97D1C5.description: Compare and contrast treatments of the same topic in several primary and secondary sources.

3D0BB34BB9C0403BAAEFD85BAEE8E412.description: Assess the extent to which the reasoning and evidence in a text support the author's claims.

51FECAE3A9224EB6A8E96A330E2F974B.description: Integrate quantitative or technical analysis (e.g., charts, research data) with qualitative analysis in print or digital text.

E450F8754B0647668F13C71CB0FC1BEE.description: Compare the point of view of two or more authors for how they treat the same or similar topics, including which details they include and emphasize in their respective accounts.

8382393A8B50484EA094876130BFCEEF.description: Analyze how a text uses structure to emphasize key points or advance an explanation or analysis.

947D64AF1ACF47E18717ADABCD8084FA.description: Determine the meaning of words and phrases as they are used in a text, including vocabulary describing political, social, or economic aspects of history/social science.

582A3E720A2045698B1B8100A0423DC9.description: Analyze in detail a series of events described in a text; determine whether earlier events caused later ones or simply preceded them.

B8BC91EF17E5408F98B95924796C4007.description: Determine the central ideas or information of a primary or secondary source; provide an accurate summary of how key events or ideas develop over the course of the text.

DED0A4A338DD4F789ABC04C94691832A.description: Cite specific textual evidence to support analysis of primary and secondary sources, attending to such features as the date and origin of the information.

standardSets.title: Grade 9-10
standardSets.subject: Writing Standards for Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

document.title: Grades 6-12 Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, & Technical Subjects

38993A5974EE47DAB3EF785D60CBA7AB.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.
